## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up at `ad2ae922`, reassessing the [previous review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12972#issuecomment-5806715260) after the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12972#issuecomment-5808507119).

**Verified:** the tmpfiles finding from the previous review is resolved, and the four findings from the [first](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12972#issuecomment-5791310535) and [second](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12972#issuecomment-5803495476) reviews have not regressed. No production defect was found in the new watcher. One optional test improvement and one low-impact behavior note follow.

| Earlier finding | Status at `ad2ae922` |
|---|---|
| The tmpfiles entry is not applied on upgrade | **Resolved.** The watcher no longer needs `/var/lib/omarchy`: inotify watches only `/dev`, the toggle still creates the directory before writing the flag, and the udev rule's `TEST` is simply false while it is missing. The tmpfiles file is gone and nothing references it. |
| Missing state directory, unrelated `/dev` opens, ancestor watch, redirection order | **Still resolved.** A failed waiter still ends in the 5s back-off. The inotify filter is narrower (`open,close` on `/dev/video*` only). No directory other than `/dev` is watched, and `omarchy-toggle-camera` is unchanged. |

**Verified, author's reply:**
- **Unplug gap: confirmed.** At `b410b57b`, unplugging a disabled camera produced no `/dev` or flag event, so the bar waited for the 30s timeout. At `ad2ae922`, the interface `remove` event wakes the watcher. In an isolated stand-in run, the bar updated about 0.1s after the event line.
- **Waiter lifecycle: confirmed** with the real `inotifywait`, `udevadm` and `setpriv` in a sandbox. Killing either waiter took down the other and the inner shell within milliseconds. The watcher restarted both after 5.0s with a stable fd count, and stopping the watcher ended everything.
- **Events seen:** writes to `authorized` emit no uevent themselves. The watcher sees driver `unbind` on disable and `bind` from the `drivers_probe` write on enable, plus `add`/`remove` on plug and unplug. The flag is written or removed before those sysfs writes, so the scan they trigger reads the new state.
- **Replug:** "never gets a `/dev` node" is overstated. Once `uvcvideo` is loaded, a replugged disabled camera is bound during enumeration and gets `/dev/videoN` briefly, before rule 70's `authorized=0` write can take effect. So `b410b57b` usually did wake on replug. This comes from kernel and systemd source, not hardware. The new code covers both cases either way; only the comments at [`omarchy-camera-status:93-95`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/ad2ae92273bf8f02cb0f5e5366954aeb703d56a4/bin/omarchy-camera-status#L93-L95) and [`camera-toggle-test.sh:138-139`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/ad2ae92273bf8f02cb0f5e5366954aeb703d56a4/test/shell.d/camera-toggle-test.sh#L138-L139) are affected.
- **Live hardware result:** not reproduced (no hardware), but consistent with the source and the stand-in run.

**Optional test improvement:** the new watch test can fail against a correct watcher. The [`inotifywait` stub](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/ad2ae92273bf8f02cb0f5e5366954aeb703d56a4/test/shell.d/camera-toggle-test.sh#L96-L100) exits at once, so `wait -n` can end the inner shell before the `udevadm` stub has logged its arguments or before its `setpriv` has set the parent-death signal:

```text
inotifywait stub exits 1 -> wait -n returns -> inner shell exits
  udevadm stub not yet logged     -> killed by pdeathsig -> "follows cameras on the USB bus" fails
  udevadm setpriv not yet armed   -> stub survives       -> "takes the udev monitor down" fails
```

The full test failed 1 of 30 runs on an unmodified head, and a harness running the script's waiter code with the test's stubs showed 17 to 38 anomalies per 3000 starts. Having the failing stub wait, with a bound, for the monitor stub to record its PID closes both races:

```bash
cat >"$watch_bin/inotifywait" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
printf 'inotifywait %s\n' "$*" >>"$WATCH_LOG"
for _ in {1..200}; do [[ -s $WATCH_PIDS ]] && break; sleep 0.01; done
exit 1
SH
```

With this change: no anomalies in 6000 harness starts, 50 of 50 full-test passes, and the test still fails with `wait` in place of `wait -n` and with the monitor started without `--pdeathsig`.

### Flag changes without a driver bind or unbind wait for the timeout

The flag file itself is no longer watched. A toggle reaches the watcher only through the `unbind`/`bind` events that its sysfs writes cause, which happen only when a driver is bound to the camera. With a camera present but no driver bound (for example a failed `uvcvideo` probe, a blacklisted driver or a manual flag edit), nothing wakes the loop. In the stand-in run, a flag-only change with a camera present did not show within 1.5s at `ad2ae922`, against 0.1s at `b410b57b`.

**Impact:** the bar can show the old on/off state for up to the 30s read timeout in that case. Ordinary toggles of a working camera are unaffected, and with no camera present the widget is hidden. How often a video interface has no bound driver was not measured. The two technical assessments differ on whether this warrants a change: one rates it low with no change needed, the other a conditional latency regression.

**Suggested change:** if the case matters, have `omarchy-toggle-camera` or the widget trigger a refresh after a toggle, rather than relying only on bind/unbind events. Not tested.
